I'm writing to apply for the Computational Biologist position at Form Bio. Over the past six years working as a bioinformatician at the Institute of Biotechnology, UNAM, I've gotten pretty good at digging into complex biological datasets, working with multi-omics data, and figuring out how to turn biological questions into code that actually works.

I have a Ph.D. in Bioinformatics and have spent a lot of time working with genomics, transcriptomics, and analyzing large datasets. I enjoy building bioinformatics pipelines using tools like Snakemake and Nextflow—I find there's something satisfying about creating workflows that just run smoothly. Most of my programming is in Python and R, and I've worked with everything from RNA-seq to whole genome sequencing data. I'm good at spotting interesting patterns in messy biological data, especially when it comes to genetic engineering projects.

What really draws me to Form Bio is how you're using AI to speed up cell and gene therapy development. I think there's huge potential in combining computational approaches with therapeutic design, and I'd love to help build tools that can make a real difference in genetic medicine. The idea of working on problems that could actually help people get better treatments is exactly what got me into this field in the first place.

You can find my portfolio and publications at www.lmgb.xyz. Thank you for your consideration.
